Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

ride verb

also go for a ride, take a ride, go for a drive, a ride

classical

Traupman 218: ride (a car, plane, train), with the ablative

vehī

ride (in or on a vehicle)

An ancient verb used for toy vehicles.

Other words

  • vectiō, vectiōnis f. — a ride, a being carried

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.151: quadrupedum vectiōnēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 218

  • gestātiō, gestātiōnis f. — a ride or drive for pleasure

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Lewis & Short s.v. gestātiō: a riding, driving or sailing for pleasure (not ante-Augustan); Traupman 215, 218

Examples

  • gestātiōnem autocīnētō facere

    to go for a ride in a carTraupman 215, 218

See also ride-on car, push, pull.

SourcesLewis & Short: vehor

Lewis & Short: vectio · Lewis & Short: gestatio

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
